content.why_title: Why Convert JSON Configuration Files to TOML?
content.why_desc: JSON is not designed for configuration files — it lacks comments, has noisy syntax for nested data, and requires extra escaping. TOML makes the same data more readable with [section] headers, # comments, and cleaner key-value syntax. Converting your config.json to config.toml improves maintainability, self-documentation, and collaboration for any project configuration.

arrays.title: ✓ Check Arrays of Objects Carefully
arrays.desc: JSON arrays of objects ([{name:"a"},{name:"b"}]) use TOML's [[array-of-tables]] syntax. Verify these convert correctly in the output.

null.title: ✓ TOML Has No null Value
null.desc: JSON's null has no direct TOML equivalent. Nulls are typically omitted or replaced with empty strings in conversion. Handle these cases manually.

keys.title: ✓ Quote Keys With Special Characters
keys.desc: TOML keys containing hyphens or spaces must be quoted: "content-type" = "json". Use underscores in JSON keys to avoid this issue.

test.title: ✓ Test With Your Application's TOML Parser
test.desc: Different TOML parsers (toml-rs, tomllib, @iarna/toml) may handle edge cases differently. Always test the converted TOML in your actual runtime environment.

faq.q1: Can all JSON data types be converted to TOML?
faq.a1: Most types convert cleanly: strings, numbers, booleans, arrays, and objects all have direct TOML equivalents. JSON null has no TOML equivalent and is typically omitted. Deeply nested object arrays may need manual adjustment.
faq.q2: Can TOML fully replace JSON for configuration files?
faq.a2: Yes, for static configuration files. Any code reading the config needs to switch from JSON.parse() to a TOML parser (toml crate in Rust, tomllib in Python, etc.). TOML cannot replace JSON for APIs or data exchange.
faq.q3: What file extension does TOML use?
faq.a3: TOML files use the .toml extension. Common examples: Cargo.toml (Rust), pyproject.toml (Python), config.toml (Hugo), .cargo/config.toml (Cargo settings).
faq.q4: How do I choose between JSON, YAML, and TOML for config?
faq.a4: Use JSON for API data exchange (universal support, no comments needed). Use YAML for DevOps config (Kubernetes, CI/CD — rich features, wide tool support). Use TOML for application config files (simplest syntax, explicit types, great for human editing).
